text:
maria: Quick sync — Sam from Atlas asked for per-region soft-fallbacks for their EU traffic. Can we fit this into next sprint or do we need a scoped playbook?
ajay: Depends on scope. Do they want per-tenant flags + region-aware routing + automatic downgrade to cheaper model?
sam-cust: Hi — primarily want: 1) keep latency < 200ms for EU, 2) if modelv2 degrade, fallback to a smaller model with preserved semantics, 3) opt-in quiet A/B for 5% of traffic. No KMS changes.
kevin: SRE here — fallback needs circuit breaker + surge slice. We should define thresholds (p95 latency, error rate) and an automated revert window.
elaine: From UX: if we do A/B, Atlas wants label + opt-out for enterprise customers. We can expose in the tenant console.
maria: Proposal: create a new feature flag "atlas.eu.soft_fallback" scoped to tenant + region. Canary with 1% -> 5% -> 20% over 48h. Fallback policy: on p95 > 250ms OR 2% 5xx for 5m -> shift affected slice to model-small.
ajay: Implementation notes: router already supports region tag. Need a small config surface: {
  "flag": "atlas.eu.soft_fallback",
  "slices": ["canary","ramp","steady"],
  "triggers": {"p95_ms":250, "error_pct":2},
  "fallback_model": "gpt-small-quant"
}
kevin: +1. Also add a cooldown TTL so it doesn't flip-flop: min-fallback-duration = 15m. And a max-fallback-per-day to avoid thrash.
rollout-bot: [deploy check] config validated for routing rule, infra quota check passed.
maria: Risk items: customer-visible rollback path, telemetry that ties prompt sets to quality regressions, and billing impact if fallback model increases token usage.
ajay: For rollout plan: we can land flag gating in a small PR, add a runtime hook in router, then a short canary run in staging. Estimated dev: 6 dev-days, qa: 2 days, infra changes: 1 day.
elaine: Design deliverables: flag UX in tenant console + toast for canary opt-in. I'll sketch tomorrow.
sam-cust: Timeline request: Atlas asks to start canary in 3 weeks. Is that realistic?
maria: With current queue, yes if we prioritize — we need a clear launch criteria doc. Launch criteria draft: 1) canary stable for 24h with <1% regressions on key prompt set, 2) no SLO violations in region for 6h, 3) rollback plan tested in staging.
kevin: Add a kill-switch: global emergency toggle and tenant-scoped kill for Atlas. Ops runbook: steps, contacts, and script snippet.
ajay: Ops script snippet: 
```
# switch atlas tenant to fallback
curl -X POST $ROUTER/admin/switch -d '{"tenant":"atlas","region":"eu","model":"gpt-small-quant"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"
```
maria: Customer comms: inform Atlas of canary windows, telemetry they'll see, and expected rollback criteria. Sam, can you confirm internal stakeholders?
sam-cust: Confirmed — security ok, legal OK. We'll notify EU product owners.
maria: Ok next steps: ajay to open PR with flag + router hook, kevin to draft runbook + thresholds, elaine to design UX, sam to coordinate Atlas comms. We'll tag this for sprint-21 prioritization.
ajay: I'll include automated test for trigger thresholds and a smoke that simulates latency spike.
kevin: I'll add alerting playbook and set up a temporary dashboard (p95, 5xx, fallback-count).
rollout-bot: Reminder: link sprint ticket to PR within 48h to keep the lane.
maria: Thanks team. If anyone sees a dependency risk ping here. :thumbsup:
